amendments.body: Rework substrate habitat area calculation so it depends on the actual substrate amount, not stored constants. Right now `SubstrateSurface` only checks whether `substrate_layers` is empty and otherwise returns the full footprint (`crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:205-209`), while `SubstrateDeep` just sums the serialized `layer.colonizable_area_cm2` values (`crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:220-225`). Those per-layer areas are precomputed as `footprint * colonizable_area_factor` without any depth term in scenario materialization (`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:748-754`), and the default layer hardcodes `100.0 cm²` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/substrate.rs:24-33`). The result is that larger tanks, deeper layers, or zero-depth layers can report the wrong substrate habitat area even after `refresh_habitat_registry()`.
amendments.rationale: This breaks the stated contract that colonizable areas are derived from geometry/substrate state, and it will mis-scale any later habitatized substrate biofilm or redox logic.

amendments.body: Derive plant crowding inside the habitat registry refresh path, or recompute `PlantGuildState.crowding_index` before every registry rebuild. `compute_habitat_registry()` attenuates habitat light from the cached `crowding_index` field (`crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:85-94`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:179`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:199`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:215`), but scenario materialization seeds every plant with a placeholder `crowding_index: 0.1` regardless of biomass or tank size (`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:783-788`), and trim actions change biomass then immediately refresh the registry without recalculating crowding (`crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:628-649`, `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:727`). That leaves `GlassHardscape`, `PlantSurfaces`, and `SubstrateSurface` light exposure stale after startup and after biomass-changing actions until the next daily plant-growth pass.
amendments.rationale: The registry is supposed to be the canonical live view of habitat modifiers; stale shading values will mislead downstream habitat consumers.

amendments.body: Use the actual water column above the substrate when computing `SubstrateSurface.light_exposure`. The current attenuation term is based on `state.geometry.mean_depth_cm()` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:117`), but `mean_depth_cm()` is just `fill_height_cm` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:60-61`), so changing substrate depth does not change substrate-surface light even though the habitat surface moves closer to or farther from the lamp. `TankState::substrate_depth_cm()` already exists (`crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:172-177`) and could be used to derive the real water depth above the substrate.
amendments.rationale: This makes one of the new habitat light modifiers insensitive to a core depth input the task was meant to model.

payload.summary: Reviewed the current habitat-registry implementation paths (`types/habitat.rs`, `state.rs`, `save.rs`, `engine.rs`, and scenario materialization). `git diff` was empty in the working tree, so I reviewed the landed code and ran `cargo test -p tank_core --test habitat_registry`, `cargo test -p tank_core --test save_load`, and `cargo test -p tank_scenarios`. I found three correctness gaps: substrate habitat areas are not derived from actual substrate amount, crowding-based light modifiers can remain stale between daily plant updates, and substrate-surface light attenuation ignores actual substrate depth.
